## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14  
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)

## SYSTEM STATUS
The system has a critical pump problem requiring immediate professional attention. The effluent pump is running but drawing no hydraulic load, indicating a mechanical failure that poses a risk of motor damage. All other components inspected during this visit are in good condition, but the pump failure prevents normal system operation and treatment.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The tank is holding fluid at the outlet level. The effluent filter was light with soiling and was cleaned and reseated during this visit.

## PUMP ASSESSMENT
| Parameter | Measured | Nameplate | Load % | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amp Draw | 1.6 A | 7.2 A | 22.2% | CRITICAL |

The pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its nameplate amperage. This indicates no hydraulic load is present. The motor is operating without fluid cooling, creating a risk of thermal damage. The most likely causes are a broken or missing impeller, a severed or disconnected discharge line, or a dry-run condition.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
The dispersal field surface is dry with no evidence of breakout or ponding.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured tank levels and recorded solids content
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm (functional)
- Verified electrical connections (sound)
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**CRITICAL - Immediate professional attention required:**
The effluent pump is operating at no load. This is a mechanical failure that must be diagnosed and repaired immediately. Do not continue operating the system in this condition. A qualified pump technician must inspect the pump discharge line for blockage or disconnection, and inspect or replace the pump impeller. Until the pump is repaired, the aerobic treatment unit cannot function and wastewater treatment is compromised.

**After pump repair:**
Once the pump has been repaired and is confirmed to be drawing normal amperage under load, resume the 12-month maintenance interval. Recommend measuring dissolved oxygen at the next maintenance visit to confirm that the aerobic treatment unit is operating effectively.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

Your system has a pump failure. The pump motor is running but is not moving water, which means wastewater is not being treated or dispersed. This is not a minor issue and cannot wait. Contact a septic service provider immediately to have the pump inspected and repaired.

The tank itself is in good condition. Solids are at a healthy level (about 23 percent of tank volume), and the filter is clean. Once the pump is fixed, your system should return to normal operation.
